title: Deploy composes backup-before-migrate before activating the candidate
description: Producer child of task-78eedd8ebc2b43c581ac21ea28648a9a, governor-directed re-slice 2026-09-06 19:10Z. Parent remains browser proof; this child closes the production forward call. At local0737f06c AND owner origin4253eba9, git grep migrateWithBackup outside tests finds only migration-service.ts:78. Engine0a56 already shipped ordering/receipt/restore; reuse, do not rebuild. Deploy service/command exist; owner origin4ac0dbda changes build/release authority and must be reconciled before implementation, never plan against old deploy wiring. Environment delivery is shipped (readEnvironmentDelivery/resolveEnvironmentLaunch); reuse explicit project/environment resolution, never launchDelivery's refusal-to-undefined convenience for required DB context. One host-context resolver composed here may be reused by migrate-down sibling, which depends on this row. No remote target or connection string from browser. definitionOfDone: A real production deployment.deploy dispatch reaches existing migrateWithBackup for the admitted project/environment and exact deploy workspace/SHA, before candidate activation or traffic flip. Test through default daemon composition with injectable bounded host effects, not an isolated call to engine.

Missing/unreadable database or mismatched target/workspace refuses before any migration effect, with stable code and actual layer. Resolve named environment values at the host boundary; never silently select production for preview, accept URL/workspace in command payload, or persist/log a secret.

Production-composition ordering arm awaits dump completion before apply; MIGRATION_BACKUP_FAILED leaves schema unchanged and prevents candidate activation/traffic flip. MIGRATION_FAILED names failing file, persists REFUSED migration receipt and prevents deployed-success claim; assert actual effect counters/schema, code+layer, not just return.

Replay/concurrency tests prove no duplicate batch or unsafe interleaving; use existing migration project lock and receipt identity, retain backup after post-dump failure, handle receipt-write/cleanup failures explicitly. No automatic schema rollback or restore beyond authority already supplied.

Default-composition test and fresh scoped daemon tests/typecheck execute with nonzero counts; full daemon/root/app gates disclosed per path and lease rules. New runtime modules have physical .js bridges. Parent78 and migrate-down composition child consume the shipped edge; no new feature sibling dependency or second migration engine.
taskRails: Reuse landed engine and owner-origin deploy authority; remeasure after reconciliation. Do not duplicate release/build authority.
Connection values remain process/host-only; no value, hash, prefix, URL, SQL or tool-output leak in evidence.
Pre-migration backups use existing .moe-next/backups/pre-migration/<env> and shared lock; no second backup location.

implementationPlan.description: MEASURE AND RECONCILE. NO EDITS. (a) RE-CONFIRM THE RECONCILIATION the description demands: `git merge-base --is-ancestor 4ac0dbda HEAD` — it was YES at planning (4ac0dbda "fix: harden release and deployment review gaps" is an ancestor of f213b41d), which means this plan is written against post-reconciliation wiring. If HEAD has moved, RE-READ the deploy sequence before trusting any line number below. (b) CONFIRM THE GAP: `git grep -n "migrateWithBackup" -- apps packages` minus `*.test.*` returns TWO hits — migration-service.ts:78 (definition) and deployment/migrate-down-test-fixtures.ts (a FIXTURE, test-tier despite the filename). There is still NO production consumer; do not mistake the fixture for a landed edge. (c) READ THE ENGINE end to end (migration-service.ts, 98 lines) and record what it ALREADY owns so you do not rebuild it: `MigrationInput` = `{projectRoot, workspace, projectId, requestId, environment, sha, databaseUrl, now?}` (:10-19); replay by `requestId` with `MIGRATION_RECEIPT_CONFLICT` on a mismatched environment/sha (:81-85); the project-wide lock spanning the receipt write (:91-93) with `MIGRATION_LOCK_LEAF` exported so the revert shares ONE lock. (d) READ THE DEPLOY SEQUENCE (deploy-service.ts) and write down the exact line of `candidateStarted = true; startCandidate` — that is the boundary your migration must precede. (e) MEASURE THE THREE ENVIRONMENT RESOLVERS and confirm the choice for yourself rather than taking it from this plan: `PURPOSE_ENVIRONMENTS` (environment-launch-resolver.ts:69-71) really is only `{PREVIEW, VERIFIER}` with no deploy member, and `launchDelivery` (:177) really does coerce refusals to `undefined`. Record the baseline for the daemon leg and typecheck.

THE HOST-CONTEXT RESOLVER — NEW `apps/daemon/src/deployment/deploy-migration-context.ts` plus its one-line `.js` bridge (DoD 5), and a NAME-MATCHED `deploy-migration-context.test.ts` in step 3 (without the matching name, runtime-entrypoint.test.ts calls the module TEST tier and reports the bridge as `unexpected`). It is a MODULE rather than an inline block because the description says the migrate-down sibling, which depends on this row, reuses it. IT RESOLVES `MigrationInput`'s host half for an ADMITTED (project, environment, workspace, sha): the project root, the workspace, and the `databaseUrl`. USE `readEnvironmentDelivery(config, environment)` (environment-delivery.ts:104), passing the deploy's ALREADY-ADMITTED environment string. DO NOT USE `resolveEnvironmentLaunch` — it derives the environment from `PURPOSE_ENVIRONMENTS` (:69-71), which is exactly `{PREVIEW: "preview", VERIFIER: "verify"}` with NO deploy member, so a production deploy would resolve some other environment's variables, which is DoD 2's "silently select production for preview" hazard arriving from the opposite direction. DO NOT USE `launchDelivery` — its own header says a refusal becomes `undefined` so the child starts WITHOUT variables, which for a required DATABASE_URL means migrating with no database context. INSPECT THE REFUSAL AND FORWARD IT UNCHANGED: `readEnvironmentDelivery` already carries the code AND the layer that answered (SCOPE for an unknown environment, KEY for an underivable seal), and restamping would report the wrong layer — that is DoD 2's "stable code and actual layer". A MISMATCHED TARGET OR WORKSPACE, OR AN ABSENT DATABASE VALUE, REFUSES HERE — before any migration effect. THE VALUE NEVER LEAVES THE PROCESS (task rail 2): no `databaseUrl` in a return summary, a log line, a refusal detail or an error message; keep it out of anything that could be serialised. Keep the module under 250 lines.

THE RESOLVER'S ARMS — NEW `apps/daemon/src/deployment/deploy-migration-context.test.ts` (the name MUST match step 2's module exactly). FIVE ARMS: (a) a readable environment resolves the full `MigrationInput` host half for the ADMITTED environment; (b) THE WRONG-ENVIRONMENT ARM, which is DoD 2's core: variables bound for `preview` are NOT returned when resolving `production`, and vice versa — assert the isolation directly rather than trusting the call; (c) an unreadable or absent store refuses with the code AND layer `readEnvironmentDelivery` returned, forwarded unchanged — assert both, per global rail 1, and assert it refuses BEFORE any migration effect; (d) a mismatched target or workspace refuses with its own stable code and layer; (e) NO SECRET LEAKS — assert that no returned value, refusal, or serialised form contains the database URL, WITH A POSITIVE CONTROL: feed a credential-shaped value and prove the assertion would have caught it. Without the control the arm passes vacuously because nothing credential-shaped was ever present, which is the failure mode epic rail 3 keeps producing on this board.

THE PORT AND THE ORDERED CALL SITE (DoD 1, 3). (1) `apps/daemon/src/deployment/deploy-ports.ts`: add a migration port to `DeployPorts` (:51-59, currently `{build, docker, releaseDecision, ssh, target, transfer}`), following the shape of the existing members — an injectable bounded host effect, so a test can drive it without a database. (2) `apps/daemon/src/deployment/deploy-service.ts` (310 lines, under the cap — add the call and its refusal branch only): call the migration AFTER the image digest is verified (`image inspect`, ~:264) and BEFORE `candidateStarted = true; startCandidate` (~:270). THAT PLACEMENT IS THE SUBJECT OF THE ROW AND IS DELIBERATE ON BOTH SIDES — write it as a comment: migrating before the build could move the schema and then fail to produce an image, leaving the schema ahead of the code; migrating after `startCandidate` boots the candidate against the OLD schema. It also mirrors the file's own principle at :229-232, that an effect with no durable trace is worse than a refusal. ON MIGRATION REFUSAL: return through the existing `refuse(...)` path so the deploy receipt records it, and DO NOT start the candidate or flip the proxy. `MIGRATION_FAILED` must NOT produce a DEPLOYED outcome (DoD 3). DO NOT re-implement replay, locking or receipt identity — `migrateWithBackup` owns all three (task rail 1), and a second lock leaf would defeat the shared lock the revert depends on.

COMPOSE THE PRODUCTION EDGE (DoD 1, 5), in `apps/daemon/src/deployment/deploy-command.ts` (252 lines). Wire the real migration port — step 2's resolver feeding `migrateWithBackup` — into the production `DeployPorts`, so a REAL `deployment.deploy` dispatch reaches it through the DEFAULT daemon composition rather than only through an injected test object. THE PRODUCTION DEFAULT MUST BE THE REAL MIGRATION: a composition that silently falls back to a no-op when no port is supplied would make every production deploy skip its migration while reporting success — the same class of defect as a fake docker default. If the port is optional in the type, prove by observation in step 6 that the default is the real one. DECLARE THE `.js` BRIDGE for any new runtime module reached from here (DoD 5). Do not duplicate release or build authority (task rail 1) — 4ac0dbda already reconciled it and this row composes rather than re-decides.

THE ORDERING, REFUSAL AND CONCURRENCY ARMS (DoD 1, 3, 4), in `apps/daemon/src/deployment/deploy-service.test.ts` and `apps/daemon/src/deployment/deploy-journey.test.ts`. Drive the REAL command edge — deploy-journey.test.ts already resolves `entries[DEPLOYMENT_DEPLOY_COMMAND_KIND].asyncHandler` and injects `ports:` at :110, and migrate-down-test-fixtures.ts:43 records the discipline: "The only doubles are the two host ports." ARMS: (a) DoD 1 — a real dispatch reaches the migration for the admitted project/environment with the exact workspace and SHA, asserted by OBSERVING the port being called with those values, through the default composition. (b) DoD 3 ORDERING — the dump COMPLETES before the apply begins; assert the observed sequence, not merely that both happened. (c) `MIGRATION_BACKUP_FAILED` leaves the schema UNCHANGED and prevents BOTH candidate activation and the traffic flip — assert the effect counters and the schema, plus code AND layer, never just the return value (DoD 3 says this explicitly). (d) `MIGRATION_FAILED` names the failing file, persists a REFUSED migration receipt, and the DEPLOY receipt does NOT read DEPLOYED. (e) DoD 4 REPLAY/CONCURRENCY — a repeated dispatch produces NO duplicate batch (the engine's `requestId` replay), and two interleaved attempts do not both apply: use the EXISTING project lock and receipt identity, and assert `MIGRATION_IN_PROGRESS` with its layer rather than a generic failure. (f) A post-dump failure RETAINS the backup, and receipt-write/cleanup failures are handled explicitly — no automatic schema rollback or restore beyond the authority already supplied.

DRILLS, GATES, SELF-REVIEW (DoD 5). DRILLS — `git status --porcelain` the mutated paths FIRST and say which proof applies to which: the four existing files are TRACKED (empty `git diff -- <path>`, in a call SEPARATE from the restore); step 2's and step 3's THREE NEW files are UNTRACKED and `git diff` is BLIND to them, so back each up out of tree (%TEMP%, suffixed with your worker id) and prove restoration by SHA256 equality (global rail 13). FOUR DRILLS: (i) THE ORDERING DRILL, the row's subject — move the migration call to AFTER `startCandidate` and confirm arm (c) reds on the candidate having been activated despite a backup failure. Quote the failing line. (ii) Swap `readEnvironmentDelivery` for `resolveEnvironmentLaunch` and confirm the wrong-environment arm (3b) reds — this is the mistake the plan exists to prevent and the drill proves the arm can see it. (iii) Coerce the refusal to `undefined` the way `launchDelivery` does, and confirm arm (3c) reds rather than the migration proceeding with no database context. (iv) Remove the production migration port from the composition and confirm the DoD-1 default-composition arm reds — proving the default is the real migration, not a silent no-op. GATES — standalone and foreground, one command per call, no pipes and no `;` chains, each quoted with its `Test Files N passed` count line; an exit-0 leg with NO count line RAN NOTHING (global rail 8): `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` and `pnpm typecheck`, plus fresh SCOPED runs of the new and edited files with NONZERO counts (DoD 5 requires nonzero executed counts). Root `pnpm test` covers no `apps/**` file — say so rather than quoting it. Disclose full-daemon/root/app results per path and per the lease rules; if the exclusive lease is contended, cite a named recent run with its anchor rather than queueing. Attribute red by HEAD minus step 1's baseline intersected with this row's owned paths.

ADVERSARIAL PASS AND COMPLETION RECORD. Load `adversarial-self-review` and read your diff as an attacker. ANSWER IN WRITING: can the database URL reach ANY durable or observable surface — grep your diff for the value flowing into a receipt, a log, a refusal detail, an error message or a test assertion, and state where it is confined (task rail 2, epic rail 3); can a deploy for `preview` ever resolve `production`'s variables, or the reverse (the `PURPOSE_ENVIRONMENTS` hazard); does a migration refusal EVER leave a candidate running or the proxy flipped; can two concurrent deploys of the same project both apply a batch, and does the answer depend on the EXISTING lock rather than a new one; does a receipt-write failure leave the lock held; is the backup retained after a post-dump failure; and would a production deploy with NO migration port configured silently skip the migration and report success. THE COMPLETION RECORD MUST STATE: that 4ac0dbda was confirmed an ancestor of HEAD, so this was built on reconciled deploy wiring; the exact placement of the migration call relative to `startCandidate` and why both neighbours are wrong; WHICH resolver was used and why the other two were rejected, naming `PURPOSE_ENVIRONMENTS`' members and `launchDelivery`'s refusal-to-undefined; that no second engine, lock leaf or replay check was added; the four drill outcomes with their failing lines and restore proofs; and the scoped runs with their nonzero counts. Name the host-context resolver module explicitly so the migrate-down sibling that depends on this row can compose it rather than writing a second one. planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
WHICH ENVIRONMENT RESOLVER — the row's central correctness question, and TWO of the three candidates are wrong for measurable reasons. The description says "reuse explicit project/environment resolution, never launchDelivery's refusal-to-undefined convenience for required DB context". Measuring the three:
- `launchDelivery` (environment-launch-resolver.ts:177) — REJECTED, and its own header says why: "A REFUSAL BECOMES `undefined` HERE... a boundary that cannot read the store starts the child WITHOUT operator variables rather than not starting it at all." For a DATABASE_URL a migration needs, that is catastrophic: an unreadable store would present as "no variables" and the migration would proceed with no database context. This is the convenience the task rail names.
- `resolveEnvironmentLaunch` (:133) — REJECTED, and this one is NOT in the description; I measured it. It derives the environment from `PURPOSE_ENVIRONMENTS` (:69-71), which is exactly `{PREVIEW: "preview", VERIFIER: "verify"}`. THERE IS NO DEPLOY OR PRODUCTION PURPOSE. A deploy of `production` has no `LaunchPurpose` at all, so calling this would either return WITHHELD or resolve some OTHER environment's variables — which IS DoD 2's "silently select production for preview" hazard, arriving from the opposite direction. Reaching for the purpose-based resolver is the obvious move and it is wrong.
- `readEnvironmentDelivery(config, environment)` (environment-delivery.ts:104) — CHOSEN. It takes the environment as an explicit STRING, so the deploy's ALREADY-ADMITTED environment flows straight through with no purpose mapping in between, and its refusal forwards code AND layer unchanged (SCOPE for an unknown environment, KEY for an underivable seal), which is precisely DoD 2's "stable code and actual layer".

WHERE THE MIGRATION SLOTS, read from the deploy sequence rather than assumed. deploy-service.ts orders: admit sha/environment (:233) -> `ports.target` (:236) -> docker version (:240) -> `acquireProxy` (:245) -> replay -> build/transfer (:253-262) -> image digest inspect (:264) -> `candidateStarted = true; startCandidate` (:270-271) -> `awaitHealthy` (:274) -> `flipProxy` (:278). DoD 1 says before candidate activation or traffic flip, so the migration goes AFTER the digest is proven and BEFORE `startCandidate`. That placement is deliberate on both sides: migrating before the build would move the schema and then possibly fail to produce an image, leaving the schema ahead of the running code; migrating after `startCandidate` would mean the candidate booted against the old schema.

A NEW MODULE, NOT AN INLINE BLOCK. The description says "One host-context resolver composed here may be reused by migrate-down sibling, which depends on this row", so the resolver is a named module with a `.js` bridge (DoD 5) and a NAME-MATCHED `.test.ts` sibling — without the matching name, runtime-entrypoint.test.ts classifies the module TEST tier and reports its bridge as `unexpected`.

I DID NOT ADD A SECOND ENGINE OR A ROLLBACK. `migrateWithBackup` already owns ordering, the project-wide lock, receipt identity and replay (migration-service.ts:78-97). This row composes it; DoD 4's "no automatic schema rollback or restore beyond authority already supplied" means a post-dump failure RETAINS the backup and refuses — it does not try to be clever.

planningNotes.risks:
1. THE WRONG RESOLVER IS THE OBVIOUS ONE. `resolveEnvironmentLaunch` looks like the right abstraction and is structurally incapable of naming a deploy environment — `PURPOSE_ENVIRONMENTS` has only PREVIEW and VERIFIER. Using it would resolve preview's variables for a production deploy, which is DoD 2's named hazard. Use `readEnvironmentDelivery` with the deploy's admitted environment string.
2. NEVER COERCE THE REFUSAL. `launchDelivery` turns an unreadable store into `undefined`, which for a required DATABASE_URL means migrating with no database context or silently skipping. Inspect the refusal and refuse with ITS code and layer.
3. ORDER IS THE SUBJECT OF THE ROW. After the image digest, before `startCandidate` (deploy-service.ts:270). Migrating earlier can leave the schema ahead of an image that never built; migrating later boots the candidate against the old schema. An arm must prove the dump COMPLETED before apply, and that MIGRATION_BACKUP_FAILED prevents activation AND the flip.
4. DO NOT REBUILD THE ENGINE (task rail 1). Replay, the project-wide lock, receipt identity and backup retention are already in migrateWithBackup. A second replay check or a second lock leaf is a second authority; `MIGRATION_LOCK_LEAF` is exported so the revert shares ONE lock.
5. NO SECRET ANYWHERE (task rail 2, epic rail 3). `databaseUrl` carries credentials. It must not appear in a receipt, a log line, a refusal detail, an error path, a test fixture or an assertion message — and a test that never had a credential-shaped value present cannot prove this, so include a POSITIVE CONTROL.
6. NEW MODULE NEEDS A `.js` BRIDGE **AND** A NAME-MATCHED `.test.ts` (DoD 5). Without the matching name, runtime-entrypoint.test.ts classifies it TEST tier and reports the bridge as `unexpected` — a red that hides inside a suite already red for foreign reasons.
7. THE FIXTURE IS NOT A CONSUMER. `migrate-down-test-fixtures.ts` imports `migrateWithBackup` and is test-tier despite not matching `*.test.*`; the production edge is still missing. Do not read it as proof the composition exists.
8. ASSERT EFFECT COUNTERS AND SCHEMA, NOT RETURN VALUES (DoD 3 says so explicitly). A refusal path that returns the right code while the schema moved is the defect these arms exist to catch.
9. THE MIGRATION FAILURE MUST NOT CLAIM A DEPLOYED SUCCESS. MIGRATION_FAILED persists a REFUSED migration receipt and the deploy must not report DEPLOYED — assert the deploy receipt's outcome, not only the migration's.
